definition: Counting sort orders integers that fall in a limited range by counting how many times each value appears, then writing them back out from those counts. It is not a comparison sort, so it can beat the n log n comparison lower bound. The range has to be modest, because the count array is as large as the range.
details: Implemented by placing values according to prefix sums of the counts, it is stable.

complexity.time: O(n + k), where k is the size of the value range.
complexity.space: O(k) for the counts, plus O(n) if the output is a separate array.

examples: Sorting exam scores that only range from 0 to 100
Sorting small integers as one pass of radix sort
